subject: Compute tiering & headroom proposal — Quantive Dedicated
messages:
From: Emma Shaw <emma@quantivelabs.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Quantive Dedicated sizing — workload profile and asks

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the quick sync earlier. Quantive is moving toward a dedicated deployment and our procurement deadline is mid-June. To make the commitment decision we need a recommended compute tiering approach that balances memory headroom for our long-context retrieval pipeline and per-token cost for high-throughput embedding requests.

Quick facts from our side:
- 60M monthly embedding calls (avg 768 tokens / call) — bursty daytime pattern (US/EU).
- 1.5M long-context text-generation calls per month (avg 30k tokens of context; often batched 4–8 requests for offline summarization).
- P95 latency requirement: embeddings <120ms, gen interactive <400ms (for small prompts), batch jobs can be multi-second.
- Data residency: US West + East.

Can you put together a short recommendation that explains:
- when to choose H100 vs A100 vs L4 within a single Dedicated reservation,
- suggested headroom / concurrency assumptions and memory sizing,
- expected token-cost tradeoffs and fallback rules (e.g., route to cheaper variant when oversized contexts are rare),
- any operations constraints (KV cache sizing, eviction policy, warmup).

If you can send a brief spreadsheet with the sizing and an ops playbook, we can take that to procurement.

Best,
Emma
Emma Shaw
Head of ML Ops | Quantive Labs
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Emma Shaw <emma@quantivelabs.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quantive Dedicated sizing — workload profile and asks

Emma — thanks for the detail. We're drafting a concise compute-tiering recommendation and ops playbook; attaching a first-pass spreadsheet (will follow up with a short runbook).

Top-level thinking (preview):
- L4: best for high-volume, short-context embeddings and low-cost interactive generations. Great for baseline throughput and cost-savings when context <8k tokens.
- A100: strong middle-ground — better memory than L4 with higher FP throughput; suitable for sustained high-throughput embedding fleets and medium-context generations.
- H100: required for large-context workloads (30k tokens) where memory and model parallelism matter; also cheaper when batching large contexts for offline jobs due to kernel throughput at 80–96k token batches.

We'll size a hybrid reservation: majority L4 slots for embeddings + A100 cluster for mixed throughput + a small pool of H100 for long-context generation and batch summarization. Ops notes will include KV cache sizing, graceful fallback to A100/L4 for small contexts, and autoscale thresholds.

Irene / Dev / Vivek — can you review the attached assumptions and add any operational constraints (eviction thresholds, expected cold-starts, replication for cross-region)?

—Michael
Michael Grant
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-04T11:31:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Quantive sizing assumptions & ops tweaks

Folks — quick internal notes before we send the client-facing summary: please keep these internal (ops constraints and pricing sensitivity).

Assumptions to codify in spreadsheet:
- Embedding profile: 60M/mo at 768 tokens -> steady-state RPS ~ 15–25 with daytime spikes to 120 RPS depending on batching. Use L4 with 1.5x concurrency headroom.
- Long-context gen: 1.5M/mo @ 30k tokens -> expected batch mode for nightly summarization (common). Live interactive gen will be small subset (~5%). For 30k-context we need H100 with >=80 GiB usable memory; plan for 1.6x memory headroom for KV/cache to avoid OOM.
- A100 as warm standby: provision A100 pool sized to absorb 30–40% of gen load when H100 capacity busy — it's not ideal for 30k tokens but acceptable for 8–16k contexts with chunking.

Sizing sketch (round numbers):
- L4 pool: 24 slots (region split 16 west / 8 east) — handles embeddings + small gen; expected utilization 60–75% with autoscale + burst.
- A100 pool: 6 slots (balanced) — handles medium contexts and overflow.
- H100 pool: 3 slots — reserved for large-context batch jobs and high-memory infer.

Operational playbook highlights:
- KV cache: allocate per-GPU 10–12 GiB for L4, 30–40 GiB for A100, 60–72 GiB for H100 depending on model. Eviction policy: LRU by session age, pinned prefixes for business-critical pipelines.
- Warm pools: maintain 1 pre-warmed slot per region for H100 to cut cold-starts to ~45s -> 8–12s for L4.
- Fallback rules: route to A100 when H100 queue > 60s; route to L4 for non-critical summarization with chunking and recombine; mark degraded in telemetry.

I'll add more precise throughput-to-token-cost estimates in the spreadsheet. Dev/Vivek, flag if these headroom numbers conflict with perf telemetry.

Thanks — Irene
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Emma Shaw <emma@quantivelabs.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Quantive Labs Procurement <procurement@quantivelabs.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Quantive dedicated compute-tiering recommendation (summary)

Hi Emma / team — attaching the sizing spreadsheet (quantive_compute_tiering_v1.xlsx) and a sample KV cache profile. Below is the executive recommendation and next steps.

Executive recommendation (short):
- Hybrid reservation: primarily L4 slots for embeddings + A100 mid-tier for throughput and mixed-gen + small H100 pool for large-context workloads. This gives you unit-cost efficiency for the 60M embedding calls while preserving SLA for 30k-token summarization.

Specifics: see spreadsheet for numbers, but headline sizing:
- L4: 24 slots (split US-W/US-E) — handles embeddings and small gen, expected cost-efficient baseline.
- A100: 6 slots — handles medium contexts, overflow from L4, and can serve as fallback for some gen workloads.
- H100: 3 slots — reserved for multi-GB KV + 30k-token batch summarization. Keep 1 pre-warmed slot per region.

Memory/headroom guidance:
- Plan 1.6x KV+model memory headroom for H100 to account for peak context + batching. For A100 and L4 use 1.3x and 1.2x respectively.

Fallback & routing rules (ops):
- SLOs: embeddings P95 <120ms — keep RPS headroom on L4 pools; if L4 queue > 60s route low-priority embedding batches to A100 to avoid tail risk.
- Long-context jobs: queue to H100; if H100 unavailable, automatically batch and chunk to A100 with integrity checks and notify on degraded quality.

Next steps / asks from Quantive to finalize spreadsheet:
- 7-day sample traffic traces with token-level histograms (embeddings + gen).
- Peak RPS windows (timezone-aware).
- Top-10 prompt families for long-context summarization to validate chunking feasibility.

Attached: quantive_compute_tiering_v1.xlsx (sizing + cost delta scenarios), kv_cache_profile_sample.json (example cache footprint per slot). Let us know and we can lock a recommended reserved capacity and an ops SLA addendum for warm pools.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
Attachments: quantive_compute_tiering_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), kv_cache_profile_sample.json (text)
From: Emma Shaw <emma@quantivelabs.com>

Date: 2028-06-06T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quantive dedicated compute-tiering recommendation (summary)

Michael / Irene — this is very helpful, thank you. Procurement likes the hybrid approach; a couple of asks before we circulate:
1) Can you include a 3-column pricing delta in the spreadsheet (reserved vs reserved+burst vs reserved+warm-prewarmed H100) so procurement can see the short-term delta vs long term unit economics?
2) We need SOC 2 scope notes for data residency and key custody (we'll loop security once we have the runbook).

I'll get the 7-day traces over by tomorrow EOD. If you can add the pricing delta and the short ops SLA (warm pool cold-start guarantees) we'll aim to finalize next week.

Best,
Emma
Emma Shaw
Head of ML Ops | Quantive Labs
